description: Focaccia Genovese is a true Ligurian masterpiece, celebrated for its irresistible crisp exterior, soft airy crumb, and signature dimples filled with fragrant olive oil and sea salt. This authentic recipe brings the sun-drenched flavors of Genoa right to your kitchen, creating a versatile bread perfect for dipping, sandwiches, or as a delightful accompaniment to any Italian meal. Infused with fresh rosemary, every bite transports you to the Italian riviera.

ingredients.notes: plus 4 tbsp for pan and topping

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the warm water, granulated sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently to dissolve the sugar and yeast, then let the mixture sit undisturbed for 5 minutes until it becomes foamy on the surface. This indicates that your yeast is active and ready.

instructions.title: Mix the Dough
instructions.text: Add the all-purpose flour and fine sea salt to the activated yeast mixture. Using a sturdy wooden spoon or a spatula, mix vigorously until all the flour is incorporated and a shaggy, sticky dough forms. Avoid overmixing; a slightly sticky dough is desirable for focaccia.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Drizzle 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil into a clean, large bowl. Transfer the sticky dough into the oiled bowl, turning it once to coat the entire surface with oil. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until the dough has visibly doubled in size. This passive rise time is crucial for flavor and texture.

instructions.title: Prepare Pan and Preheat Oven
instructions.text: While the dough completes its first rise, drizzle 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil into a 9x13 inch baking pan (or similar size). Gently transfer the risen dough to the oiled pan. Use your fingertips to gently stretch and press the dough to roughly fill the pan. Preheat your oven to 425F (220C) during this step.

instructions.title: Dimple and Top
instructions.text: Uncover the dough in the pan. Drizzle the surface generously with the remaining 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil. Using your oiled fingertips, create deep dimples all over the dough's surface, pressing all the way down to the bottom of the pan. Evenly sprinkle the fresh rosemary leaves and coarse sea salt over the dimpled dough.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Bake
instructions.text: Let the dough rest in the pan for a final 15-20 minutes while your oven finishes preheating. This brief second rise helps to achieve a light, airy texture. Transfer the focaccia to the preheated oven and bake for 25-35 minutes, rotating the pan halfway through, until the focaccia is golden brown, crisp on the outside, and cooked through. Serve warm.

tips: Do not overwork the dough; a slightly sticky, soft dough yields a more tender and airy focaccia. Minimal kneading is key.
Always use high-quality extra virgin olive oil, as its rich, fruity flavor is central to authentic Focaccia Genovese.
Focaccia is best enjoyed warm on the day it is baked. If serving later, reheat briefly in a preheated oven to restore its crispness.
article:
Focaccia Genovese, a culinary masterpiece from the sun-drenched region of Liguria, Italy, is far more than just bread. It’s an experience, a symphony of simple, high-quality ingredients harmonizing to create something truly extraordinary. Imagine a flatbread with a perfectly crisp, golden crust, a wonderfully airy and chewy interior, and a fragrant aroma of fresh rosemary and rich olive oil. This is the hallmark of authentic Focaccia Genovese. Whether enjoyed for breakfast with a cup of coffee, as an afternoon snack, or as a delightful accompaniment to a meal, its versatility and irresistible flavor make it a beloved staple. If you’re ready to bring a piece of Italian tradition into your kitchen, join us as we unlock the secrets of an authentic Focaccia Genovese recipe, focusing on that signature rosemary and olive oil essence.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?
Hailing from Genoa, the capital of Liguria, Focaccia Genovese is a specific type of focaccia distinguished by its unique texture and preparation. Unlike some thicker, bread-like focaccias, the Genovese version is typically flatter, boasting a delightful crispness on the outside and a tender, open crumb within. Its defining characteristic is the generous use of extra virgin olive oil, both in the dough and drizzled lavishly over the top before baking. This olive oil, combined with a salty brine often brushed on the surface, creates those iconic "buchi" or dimples that hold pockets of deliciousness. The rosemary, often fresh and finely chopped, infuses the bread with an earthy, aromatic perfume that perfectly complements the olive oil. This isn't just a side dish; in Genoa, it’s often eaten plain, perhaps dipped in milk or coffee, showcasing its inherent deliciousness and simple elegance.

## Ingredients for Focaccia Genovese
Crafting the perfect Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil requires attention to quality ingredients. Each component plays a vital role in achieving that authentic taste and texture.

*   **Flour:** 500g Tipo 00 flour (or strong bread flour with 12-14% protein) – essential for a good crumb structure.
*   **Water:** 350-400ml warm water (around 35-40°C or 95-105°F) – adjust based on flour absorption, aiming for a very wet, sticky dough.
*   **Yeast:** 7g active dry yeast (or 20g fresh yeast).
*   **Salt:** 10g fine sea salt for the dough, plus extra coarse sea salt for sprinkling on top.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** 50-60ml high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the dough, plus an additional 50-70ml for the pan, brushing, and dimpling. This is non-negotiable for flavor.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** 2-3 sprigs, finely chopped, for infusing that signature aroma.
*   **Brine (optional but recommended):** 2 tablespoons water mixed with 1 teaspoon fine sea salt. This contributes to the dimples and a salty crust.

## Step-by-Step Focaccia Genovese Instructions
Ready to embark on making your own Focaccia Genovese recipe? This process requires patience, but the rewards are truly magnificent.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a small bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and a pinch of sugar (optional, but helps activate the yeast). Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** In a large bowl, combine the flour and the 10g of fine sea salt. Pour in the activated yeast mixture and the 50-60ml of olive oil. Mix with a spoon or your hand until a shaggy, very sticky dough forms. Do not over-knead; a brief mix is sufficient for this high-hydration dough.
3.  **First Rise (Bulk Fermentation):** Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size. For a more developed flavor, you can refrigerate it for 8-12 hours for a cold fermentation.
4.  **Prepare the Pan:** Generously coat a large baking tray (approx. 30x40cm or 12x16 inches) with a good amount of extra virgin olive oil (about 30-40ml).
5.  **Transfer and Stretch:** Gently pour the risen dough onto the oiled baking tray. Using your oiled fingertips, gently stretch the dough to cover the bottom of the pan. Don't force it; if it springs back, let it rest for 10-15 minutes and try again.
6.  **Second Rise:** Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let the dough rise again for 30-45 minutes, or until noticeably puffy.
7.  **Create Dimples and Season:** Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). Once the dough has risen, generously drizzle another 20-30ml of extra virgin olive oil over the surface. Dip your fingers in the optional brine (or just water) and firmly press them all over the dough to create deep dimples. Don't be shy! These dimples are crucial for holding the olive oil and creating that characteristic texture. Sprinkle generously with fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt.
8.  **Bake:** Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp on top and bottom. If your oven bakes unevenly, rotate the pan halfway through.
9.  **Cool:** Once baked, immediately transfer the focaccia to a wire rack to cool slightly. Brushing with a little more olive oil while warm is a secret for extra flavor and shine.

Follow this Focaccia Genovese recipe carefully for the best results.

## Tips for Perfect Focaccia Genovese
Mastering this Focaccia Genovese recipe means paying attention to a few crucial details that elevate it from good to truly exceptional.

*   **Quality Olive Oil:** This cannot be stressed enough. Use the best extra virgin olive oil you can afford. It’s a primary flavor component.
*   **Hydration is Key:** The dough is meant to be very wet and sticky. Resist the urge to add more flour during mixing or stretching. Embrace the stickiness; it contributes to the airy crumb.
*   **Patience with Rising:** Don't rush the fermentation process. Adequate rising time develops flavor and texture. Cold fermentation is a game-changer if you have the time.
*   **Deep Dimples:** Really press your fingers into the dough to create those deep indentations. They are designed to catch and hold the olive oil and brine, resulting in pockets of intense flavor.
*   **Generous Salt:** The coarse sea salt on top provides a delightful crunch and balances the richness of the olive oil. Don't skimp!
*   **Hot Oven:** A hot oven ensures a quick rise and a crispy crust.

## Serving Suggestions for Focaccia
Once you’ve perfected this Focaccia Genovese recipe, the possibilities for enjoyment are endless.

*   **Breakfast/Snack:** Enjoy it plain with a cup of coffee or cappuccino, as is traditional in Liguria.
*   **Appetizer:** Serve alongside a platter of cured meats, cheeses, and olives.
*   **Dipping:** It’s fantastic for dipping into high-quality balsamic vinegar and olive oil, or a rich tomato soup.
*   **Sandwiches:** Slice it horizontally and fill with your favorite deli meats, cheeses, or roasted vegetables for an incredible sandwich.
*   **Accompaniment:** It makes a perfect side for salads, stews, or grilled meats, soaking up all the delicious juices.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Focaccia Genovese Rosemary Olive Oil is perfection, you can certainly experiment with variations.

*   **Toppings:** Before baking, consider adding other toppings to the dimples: cherry tomatoes (halved), thinly sliced onions, black olives, or even a sprinkle of Parmesan cheese.
*   **Herbs:** While rosemary is traditional, fresh thyme or oregano can also be used, or a mix of Italian herbs.
*   **Flour:** For a slightly nuttier flavor, you can substitute a small portion (up to 10-15%) of the Tipo 00 flour with whole wheat flour, though this will slightly alter the texture.
*   **Gluten-Free:** While challenging to replicate the exact texture, gluten-free flour blends designed for bread can be used, but expect a denser crumb.
*   **Sweet Focaccia:** A less common but delicious variation involves sprinkling sugar and perhaps some grapes or figs before baking for a sweet treat.

Armed with this comprehensive Focaccia Genovese recipe, you’re now ready to embark on a delightful culinary journey. The aroma of baking focaccia, rich with rosemary and olive oil, will fill your home, and the taste of this authentic Italian bread will transport you straight to the sun-drenched Ligurian coast. Enjoy the process, savor the flavors, and share the joy of homemade Focaccia Genovese!
